# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Blind cannot see the bomb or gestures, but can hear speech and perform the bomb actions (cutting wires 1, 2, or 3). 

The turn order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf.
- Deaf can see the bomb and speak, but cannot hear.
- Mute can hear speech, read the manual, and gesture, but cannot speak.
- Blind can hear speech and act on the bomb, but cannot see.

To coordinate:
1. Deaf will observe the bomb and speak the description (which Mute and Blind can hear).
2. Mute will consult the manual and gesture the wire to Deaf.
3. Deaf will see Mute's gesture and speak the instruction to Blind.
4. Blind will cut the wire.

I will inform Mute of my readiness and confirm the protocol.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut wires 1, 2, or 3. Deaf cannot hear us, but can see the bomb and speak. When Deaf describes the bomb, check your manual and gesture the wire number to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to me.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is yellow. Three WIRES: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is blue. Mute: please consult the manual and gesture to me. Use ? for Wire 1, ? for Wire 2, ? for Wire 3, or ? / ? for other actions. Blind: wait for Mute's gesture, which I will read and speak aloud to you so you can perform the action.

Deaf has read out the bomb's state: Display 0, Yellow light, Wire 1 yellow, Wire 2 green, Wire 3 blue. Deaf also offered gesture conventions to Mute, which Mute (who can see) has received. 

In this round (Round 2), Mute has already taken their turn (gesturing to Deaf). I am Blind, and Deaf acts after me in Round 2. Deaf will see Mute's gesture and speak the instruction to me, which will arrive at the start of Round 3.

Therefore, I should wait for Deaf's vocal confirmation before cutting any wire.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute just gestured thumbs down (NO / ?) to your question or action! Do not proceed. Also, the LIGHT just turned RED. Display is still 0. Wires are 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue. Mute: I cannot hear Blind. If you need to instruct Blind, use: ?=1, ?=2, ?=3, ?=Yes/Press, ?=No/Do not press, ?/?/?/? for directions. Please gesture your instruction for Blind now.

I will wait for Deaf to observe Mute's gesture and speak the instruction to me.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status update: LIGHT is now PURPLE. DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue. Mute just gestured: ? (NO / not yet / negative). Blind: if you are asking Mute questions or waiting for an indicator/color to act, Mute's answer right now is NO (?). I will announce the light color and display every turn so you both have the exact timing.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf relays your gestures to me by voice. Deaf reported you gestured thumbs down twice. If you are waiting for a specific light color or display number before cutting, please gesture to Deaf which wire to cut (1, 2, or 3) as soon as the right condition is met, so Deaf can call it out to me.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status: LIGHT is now GREEN. DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue. Mute gestured ? (thumbs down / NO). Blind: Mute is still signaling NO. Mute: if you want to tell Blind to cut a wire, use ? (wire 1), ? (wire 2), or ? (wire 3). If you want Blind to press a button, gesture ?. If Blind asked a yes/no question, the answer is NO.

I will remind Mute of the gesture conventions and reassure them that Deaf will relay their gesture to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf reports your gestures to me each round. Remember the wire gestures for Deaf: ☝ for Wire 1, ✌ for Wire 2, 🤟 for Wire 3. If you are waiting for a specific light color or display number, continue gesturing 👎 until the condition is met, then gesture the wire number to Deaf.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute just gestured ? (TWO / Wire 2)! Wire 2 is GREEN. Current bomb state: LIGHT is ORANGE, DISPLAY is 0. Wires: 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue. Mute signaled ?, indicating action on #2 (cut wire 2 / green wire).

I received the instruction: Mute gestured ✌ (Wire 2), which Deaf communicated clearly. I will now perform the action of cutting wire 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
